question: Within a bounded v1.3 static read set, does wonder item 200, Pyramids of Egypt, reach an exact government-availability predicate, government-state read or write, display consumer, completion consumer, or AI consumer?

scope.boundary: This packet tests exact references and split-address materialization for the Pyramids record, description, cost cell, technology table, ownership bitsets, and accepted government helpers, then attempts three exact candidate decompilations and one capped item-200 scalar scan. It does not inspect the filtered scalar functions, expand truncated bodies, search every wonder or government consumer, reconstruct display, or claim executable-wide absence.

dependencies.use: Provides exact item 200 identity, record, effect-description text, and signed cost factor.
Provides the ordinary BuildingWonderProductionCostLookup path that is excluded from effect evidence.
Provides accepted technology table, ownership, eligibility, and acquisition anchors without making them Pyramids effects.

acceptedAnchors.qualification: The English description and government technology IDs are discovery hints, not effect evidence.

referenceScan.qualification: Zero reference-manager results do not prove absence because the current listing omits many split constants and undecoded paths.

splitAddressScan.negative: No split construction matched the exact Pyramids description, cost cell, or technology ownership-bitset base within the decoded listing.

candidateResults.seed: materializes the exact Pyramids record base
candidateResults.result: The decompiler recovered only a prefix and stopped on bad instruction data.
candidateResults.stop: The truncated body cannot support a completion, display, AI, or government-state claim.

candidateResults.result: The decompiler recovered a recursive table-walk prefix and stopped on bad instruction data.
candidateResults.stop: No item-200 or record-derived argument reaches the recovered prefix, and expansion past truncation is forbidden.

candidateResults.seed: directly calls both TechnologyOwnershipQuery and TechnologyEligibilityPredicate
candidateResults.result: The decompiler recovered a bounded technology-loop prefix and stopped on bad instruction data.
candidateResults.stop: The recovered prefix contains no item-200 or Pyramids-record carrier, and the exact body is truncated.

itemIdScan.result: The filtered decoded-instruction scan reached the eight-function cap and reported additional matches. None of the emitted functions was promoted as a Pyramids candidate or decompiled after the hard stop.
itemIdScan.qualification: An earlier unrestricted scalar pass was rejected because seven emitted uses were displacement 0xC8 rather than item identity. The mnemonic-filtered result is a discovery boundary, not an effect negative for its functions.

ordinaryCostBoundary.result: The accepted item-200 cost path remains ordinary wonder production-cost evidence and is not treated as completion or effect consumption.
ordinaryCostBoundary.qualification: Cost selection alone cannot prove government availability, completion, display, or AI behavior.

boundedNegative.result: The completed bounded read set does not establish an exact Pyramids-to-government-predicate, government-state, completion, display, or AI edge.
boundedNegative.limits: This negative covers the exact reference targets, the five split-address targets, and the recovered prefixes of 0x82CF0268, 0x82CEF7A0, and 0x82CF81C8. It does not classify the capped item-200 scalar functions or any undecoded, indirect, or unsearched function.
boundedNegative.falsificationCondition: A complete exact function or independently bounded dataflow joins item 200 or record-derived state to a government predicate or state mutation, completion, display, or AI consumer.

currentEvidence.method: Five sequential foreground read-only Ghidra queries: exact references, capped split constants, three exact function decompilations, one rejected unrestricted scalar diagnostic, and a mnemonic-filtered scalar-use scan.

entries.result: Record, description, cost, technology-table, ownership-bitset, and acquisition targets have zero reference-manager entries; ownership and eligibility helpers expose only the listed direct calls.
Only 0x82CF0268 materializes the record base and only 0x82CEF7A0 materializes the technology table; the scan did not truncate.
All three exact candidates truncate on bad instruction data, activating the packet stop before positive promotion.
The filtered scan emitted eight functions and reported truncation; no candidate expansion followed.

currentEvidence.qualification: The current Ghidra project and flat image match the accepted v1.3 contract and were queried read-only without a project lock. No generated-code discovery, runtime probe, or indirect-target inference was used.

guards: Do not claim that no Pyramids consumer exists outside the bounded read set.
Do not infer effect execution from the English description or government technology names.
Do not treat ordinary cost selection through 0x82CF1278 as completion or effect evidence.
Do not classify the eight emitted scalar-use functions without a new bounded discriminator.
Do not expand truncated functions, dynamic dispatch, unresolved writers, display reconstruction, runtime behavior, save or network behavior, or implementation design.
conclusion: The bounded v1.3 static read set did not establish an exact Pyramids government-availability, government-state, completion, display, or AI edge. Exact and split-address scans found only one record-base materializer and one technology-table materializer, while the shared technology helper candidate and both materializers truncate on bad instruction data. A filtered item-200 scalar scan reached its eight-function cap and remains unclassified. This is not an executable-wide absence claim.
